name: security-trusted-types-policy-review
intent: Trusted Types policy creation and trust at DOM injection sinks
artifacts: Effective require-trusted-types-for/trusted-types policy, policy factories, default policy, sink consumer and browser support.
trace: Trace an attacker-controlled value through createHTML/createScriptURL or the default policy into the protected sink. Determine whether the factory sanitizes the actual context or merely wraps input.
experiment: Use an owned DOM fixture with a benign execution marker and legitimate rich content; compare raw strings with values produced by the real policy factory.
disproof: A TrustedHTML object is not proof of sanitization. An unsupported browser or unenforced policy cannot prove the protected configuration failed.
repair: Constrain policy creation and repair the factory/consumer, then verify rejected untrusted markup and preserved intended rendering.
branch_decisions: Identify which factory and output type reaches the sink: TrustedHTML is not TrustedScriptURL. An unsafe default policy can convert raw strings and must be traced separately from named factories. Policy-name allowlisting controls factory creation; it does not certify that the approved factory sanitizes its input.
operational_method: Record the sink type, assignment result/exception, selected default or named factory and resulting DOM or script URL. A raw string TypeError is different from a default policy transforming the same input into an accepted typed value. Exercise the real factory on legitimate content and an inert untrusted marker; policy creation or a TrustedHTML label alone supplies no sanitization oracle.
